'''The New York Number Theory Seminar''' is a research [[seminar]] devoted to [[number theory|theory of numbers]] and related parts of [[mathematics]] and [[physics]].

The seminar began in 1982 under the founding organizers Harvey Cohn, [[Chudnovsky brothers|David and Gregory Chudnovsky]], and [[Melvyn B. Nathanson]]. It is held at the [[Graduate Center, CUNY]].

== Overview ==
[[File:CUNY Graduate Center by David Shankbone.jpg|thumb|The [[Graduate Center, CUNY|Graduate Center]], where the New York Number Theory seminars take place, is located in the former [[B. Altman and Company Building]] at 365 Fifth Avenue.]]

The New York Number Theory Seminar began in January 1982 and was originally organized by number theorists Harvey Cohn, [[Chudnovsky brothers|David and Gregory Chudnovsky]], and Melvyn B. Nathanson.<ref name="official">{{cite web |url=https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~bumby/nyntsem/ |title=New York Number Theory Seminar |website=Richard T. Bumby |accessdate=19 March 2022}}</ref> Since the retirement of Cohn, Nathanson is the sole organizer.<ref name="official"/> The seminar also organizes an annual Workshop on Combinatorial and Additive Number Theory (CANT) at the [[Graduate Center, CUNY]].{{citation needed|date=March 2022}}

== Publications ==
Four volumes of the collected lecture notes of the seminar were published in the ''[[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]]'' series by [[Springer-Verlag]].<ref name="official"/> These volumes covered the seminar from 1982 to 1988.<ref name="official"/> Three additional stand-alone books were published by Springer-Verlag under the title ''Number Theory'', covering the seminar between 1989 and 2003.<ref name="official"/>
